highlights: Even if you are not the biggest Allen fan, it is difficult to argue against the four-time Pro Bowler having significantly more arm talent than Shough. With better receiving talent around him and holes across this Detroit defense, expect plenty of passing success and for the 253.5 passing yard line not to be nearly high enough. For the sake of the article, we will stick to the standard passing prop, but some alternate lines also stand out for the Bills’ star, such as 280+ passing yards at +170 odds on DraftKings Sportsbook. Jahmyr Gibbs Over 90.5 Rushing Yards (-110) There is plenty of talent across this Lions’ offense, but it has become increasingly evident that Jahmyr Gibbs is the foundation of the attack. After splitting carries with David Montgomery to start his career, Detroit now leans on the Alabama product as their bell-cow back. Gibbs tallied a career-high and NFL-leading 29 carries in Week 1, turning these opportunities into 156 yards and two touchdowns. Buffalo holds plenty of defensive concerns of their own entering this matchup.

Lions vs. Bills NFL Player Prop Bets and Picks for Thursday Night Football Week 2 of NFL action kicks off with a thrilling Thursday Night Football battle between the Detroit Lions and the Buffalo Bills. Both teams have deep playoff aspirations and picked up Week 1 victories. The Bills fended off the Texans 36-31, while the Lions were pushed to the limit in a 31-30 overtime victory against the Saints. They will now square off in a measuring stick matchup against each other to kick off the second week of the season. Looking at the odds, the Bills enter as 5.5-point favorites with -230 Moneyline odds on DraftKings Sportsbook. The Lions hold +190 odds to pull off the upset, with the game total set at 54.5 points. But there are plenty of ways to get involved in the action beyond backing a side or total. Let’s take a look at my top three favorite player props for the Week 2 Thursday Night Football matchup. Lions vs. Bills NFL Player Prop Bets for Thursday Night Football

This is a Texans’ defense that finished last season ranked second in opponents’ points allowed, first in yards conceded, and sixth in opponents’ passing yards last season. They were widely expected to have a case for one of the top defensive units in football this year, but will need to make some major improvements from their Week 1 performance if this is to be the case. But the impressive output should say more about Allen than the Texans’ defense. The Bills’ star had a bit of a down season last year in his passing metrics, averaging 215.8 passing yards per game. But he is averaging 235.9 passing yards per game in his career and tallied as many as 284.0 over a season. Allen still tallied 253 passing yards or greater in seven games ,even with it being a down year in passing production last year. Allen will also be able to feast on this Lions’ defense, given the concerns mentioned above. Tyler Shough aired the ball out for 410 passing yards and three touchdowns against them last week to provide the upset scare.

I doubt Cleveland has many plans to give him designed runs at all, outside of the odd QB sneak. That means the majority of his rushing would come from QB scrambles. The small sample size we have shows there's a meaningful 10% or more (up to 30%-40%) dock in scrambling yards per carry in QBs and older RBs. With no injury, I'd be projecting Watson at around 20.5 yards on average, which is a slight decline from his already declining rushing yards per game in the three years prior to his injury, and that's potentially a bit generous.

A QB's raw INT% is notoriously noisy year to year, so the fact that his INT% dipped from 2.7% over his career and 2.8% in 2024 down to 2.0% in 2025 is more a reflection of luck given the number of times he should have been picked (north of 15 times) than any real reduction in his true interception rate.
